blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275$\times$ less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Text-to-image (T2I) generation maps natural-language descriptions to images.
Modern T2I systems have an ingrained reliance on internet-scale language pretraining 1 1 1 Throughout this paper, language pretraining refers to pretraining on web-scale text-only corpora, excluding image-paired captions. for semantic conditioning of image generators.
This dependence is realized via two designs, distinguished by how and when text tokens interact with image tokens:
(1) Late fusion , the predominant design, uses two separate models: a large model is pretrained on text, and the resulting text embeddings are used to condition a separate image generator through cross- or joint attention ( Saharia et al., 2022 ; Chen et al., 2024 ; Black Forest Labs, 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) ;
(2) Early fusion removes the separate text encoder while retaining language pretraining within a single multimodal model trained on text-only and image-text data, with captions used as a prefix to condition image generation ( Team et al., 2024a ; Wang et al., 2026 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) .
Across both designs, language pretraining dominates the compute budget, accounting for over 80% of total pretraining FLOPs in representative T2I systems ( Sun et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) .
This raises two issues. First, its contribution to T2I generation has not been systematically quantified.
Second, language pretraining cost is often excluded, understating the total cost of building a T2I system.

blocks.en:
In this work, we show that strong T2I generation can be achieved without language pretraining.
We introduce Halcyon , a family of early-fusion autoregressive models that learn text conditioning directly from image–text pairs using next-token prediction.
We quantify the contribution of language pretraining to T2I generation using GPIC ( Chandrasegaran et al., 2026 ) , a dataset of 100M image–text pairs, through three experimental axes: (1) From-scratch pretraining: we train all components from scratch, including the text and image tokenizers and the generative model; (2) Data composition and scheduling: under a fixed pretraining budget, we control the mixture and schedule of text-only, T2I, and I2T examples and measure their effect on T2I generation quality; and (3) Compute comparisons: we pretrain representative T2I baselines on GPIC and compare generation quality as a function of total pretraining compute, decomposed into language and vision.
Through these experiments, we quantify the utility of language pretraining for T2I generation.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Modern T2I systems use large-scale language pretraining through two designs. In late fusion , the predominant paradigm, a language model is pretrained separately on text-only data, and its embeddings condition a visual generator. Imagen ( Saharia et al., 2022 ) , Fluid ( Fan et al., 2025 ) and PixArt- α \alpha ( Chen et al., 2024 ) use T5-XXL ( Chung et al., 2024 ) , LlamaGen-T2I ( Sun et al., 2024 ) uses T5-XL, SANA ( Xie et al., 2025 ) uses Gemma-2B ( Team et al., 2024b ) and PixelGen ( Ma et al., 2026 ) uses Qwen3-1.7B.
In early fusion , the separate text encoder is removed, but text-only pretraining is incorporated into multimodal pretraining. Chameleon ( Team et al., 2024a ) , Transfusion ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) , and Emu3 ( Wang et al., 2026 ) train jointly on text-only and image–text data, while Tuna-2 ( Liu et al., 2026 ) and SimpleAR ( Wang et al., 2025 ) initialize from
pretrained Qwen models.
Figure 2 compares the text and vision tokens used to pretrain these T2I systems.
Systems with language pretraining consume 10 12 ∼ 10 14 10^{12}\sim 10^{14} text tokens, often exceeding the vision budget. In contrast, Halcyon uses no text-only language pretraining; its only language supervision comes from caption tokens paired with images, more than two orders of magnitude lower than the language-pretraining budgets shown.
We note that early T2I systems such as DALL-E, CogView, and GLIDE learned text conditioning directly from paired image–text data, without language pretraining ( Ramesh et al., 2021 ; Ding et al., 2021 ; Nichol et al., 2022 ) .
However, the role of language pretraining has been debated: Imagen ( Saharia et al., 2022 ) found benefits from scaling pretrained text encoders, whereas Parti ( Yu et al., 2022 ) found that text-encoder pretraining only marginally reduced T2I generation loss.
Similarly, Zhang et al. (2024) found limited benefits from initializing autoregressive T2I models with pretrained language models.
Nevertheless, modern T2I systems have largely shifted toward pretrained language models for text conditioning.
We quantify the role of language pretraining and show that T2I models trained entirely from scratch, without language pretraining, can outperform strong T2I baselines relying on language pretraining.

We use four sequence formats for pretraining shown in Figure 3 .
Text-only sequences are packed, while image-containing sequences
are padded to a fixed length with [PAD] tokens. We do not pack multiple image–caption pairs
into a sequence.
For image-only (I) sequences, image tokens are predicted from [SOV] .
For image-to-text (I2T) sequences, image tokens are
predicted first, followed by caption tokens conditioned on the image.
For text-to-image (T2I) sequences, image tokens are predicted
conditioned on the caption.
For classifier-free guidance (CFG) ( Ho and Salimans, 2022 ) ,
we adopt the standard practice of dropping the caption from a fraction p drop p_{\mathrm{drop}} of T2I examples to train the unconditional branch.

blocks.en:
To measure the utility of language pretraining for T2I generation, we control the composition and scheduling of text-only, T2I, and I2T examples under a fixed pretraining budget.
Figure 4 illustrates the five configurations.
Unless otherwise specified, caption dropout is applied to T2I examples during training at rate p drop p_{\mathrm{drop}} . • Baseline T2I. We train exclusively on T2I examples. • Staged: Language → \rightarrow T2I. We allocate the first α \alpha fraction of training to text-only pretraining, followed by T2I for the remaining 1 − α 1-\alpha fraction.

This setup studies language-first pretraining schedules used in early-fusion systems such as Tuna-2 ( Liu et al., 2026 ) .
Separately, we evaluate continual pretraining recipe from an internet-scale pretrained LLM by expanding its vocabulary with image tokens and continuing training on paired image–text data. • Staged: I2T → \rightarrow T2I. We allocate the first β \beta fraction of training to I2T, followed by T2I for the remaining 1 − β 1-\beta fraction. • Mixing: T2I + I2T. We interleave T2I and I2T examples throughout training, allocating a fraction η \eta to I2T and 1 − η 1-\eta to T2I. • Mixing: T2I without caption dropout + I2T. We set η = p drop \eta=p_{\mathrm{drop}} and disable caption dropout. This preserves the baseline’s conditional and unconditional image-training tokens while additionally providing I2T supervision.

Late-fusion methods. Late fusion is the predominant design choice for modern T2I systems.
Selecting baselines for this study is non-trivial: existing systems differ in pretraining objective, language conditioning, image representation, and training setup, while our study requires public pretraining code and models that enable controlled interventions to study the role of language pretraining.
We select two representative families, LlamaGen ( Sun et al., 2024 ) and JiT-T2I ( Li and He, 2026 ; Ma et al., 2026 ) .
They cover (i) autoregressive and diffusion-based generation,
(ii) encoder-decoder and decoder-only language models of different sizes,
and (iii) image sequence lengths of 256 and 1,024.
For both families, we use the authors’ official codebases and follow their training configurations unless stated otherwise.

blocks.en:
Early-fusion methods. Existing early-fusion models, including Chameleon ( Team et al., 2024a ) and Emu3 ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , incorporate language pretraining into multimodal generative modeling.
We study the role of language pretraining in two controlled settings.
First, we vary the composition and scheduling of text-only, T2I, and I2T sequences within Halcyon under a fixed pretraining budget (Section 3.3 ).
Second, we study continual pretraining by initializing from Qwen3-0.6B-Base, pretrained on 36T text tokens, expanding its vocabulary with image tokens, and continuing pretraining on GPIC using the baseline T2I recipe.
For comparison, we train the same architecture and vocabulary from scratch under an identical T2I pretraining budget.
We disable weight decay for embedding parameters when vocabulary size is large (216K).

T2I generation without language pretraining. We now address the central question of this work: can a T2I model trained entirely from scratch match or surpass strong late-fusion systems that rely on pretrained language models? Halcyon -0.52B, a single multimodal model trained entirely from scratch, achieves 48.0 gFD, outperforming LlamaGen-XL/8 with pretrained FLAN-T5-XL (63.3) and approaching JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ with pretrained Qwen3-1.7B (41.0).
Increasing Halcyon to 1.6B parameters further reduces gFD to 35.3, surpassing both late-fusion methods.
At 4B parameters, gFD decreases to 28.4.
On compositional generation benchmarks, Halcyon -0.52B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ on GenEval (44.9 vs. 43.2) and matches its DPG-Bench score (76.84 vs. 76.85).
At 1.6B, Halcyon surpasses JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ on both GenEval (53.5 vs. 43.2) and DPG-Bench (77.9 vs. 76.9).
Moreover, Halcyon -1.6B achieves these results with 275 × \times less total pretraining compute than JiT-T2I-XXL/8++.
Together, these results demonstrate that strong T2I generation capabilities can be learned from paired image–text data alone, without language pretraining, while substantially reducing total pretraining compute.

blocks.en: 4.3 Results: Effect of Language Pretraining on T2I generation
blocks.zh: 4.3 (中文(简体) ). 结果:语言预训对T2I生成的影响

blocks.en:
External language pretraining does not improve T2I generation. We investigate this through two controlled interventions.
First, under a fixed pretraining budget, allocating α = 0.1 , 0.2 , 0.5 \alpha{=}0.1,0.2,0.5 to text-only pretraining reduces paired image–text training and worsens gFD from 48.0 to 51.6, 52.8, and 65.1, respectively; conditional image-token NLL also increases (Table 6 ).
To isolate the effect of language pretraining from reduced T2I training, we additionally evaluate language pretraining followed by a full T2I epoch ( 1.5 × 1.5\times total compute), but gFD does not improve (48.0 vs. 49.2).
Second, we investigate continual pretraining from Qwen3-0.6B-Base, pretrained on 36T text tokens.
Despite this extensive language pretraining, Qwen3-0.6B-CPT performs similar to the same architecture trained from random initialization (47.8 vs. 46.6 gFD).
Reducing the peak learning rate from 7.5 × 10 − 4 7.5\times 10^{-4} to 1 × 10 − 4 1\times 10^{-4} for continual pretraining also fails to improve T2I generation (Table 7 ).
Together, these experiments show that external text-only pretraining provides no benefit to T2I generation under the evaluated settings.

blocks.en: 4.4 Results: Effect of I2T Supervision on T2I generation
blocks.zh: 4.4 (中文(简体) ). 结果:I2T监督对T2I生成的影响

blocks.en:
I2T supervision as an additional task does not improve T2I generation. We investigate whether adding I2T supervision as a separate task through staged or mixed training improves T2I generation under a fixed pretraining budget (Table 8 ).
At an I2T allocation of 0.1 0.1 , both schedules achieve gFD comparable to the T2I baseline (48.4 and 48.2 vs. 48.0).
Increasing the allocation to 0.5 0.5 reduces conditional image tokens by half (92.2B → \rightarrow 46.1B), with staged training outperforming mixing (54.2 vs. 76.0 gFD), although neither improves upon the baseline.
Conversely, mixing substantially reduces conditional text NLL compared to staging (1.009 vs. 20.437), indicating better image captioning.
These results suggest that allocating part of the pretraining budget to I2T as a separate task does not benefit T2I generation, despite improving captioning.

在0.1 0.1的I2T分配中,两个附表都实现了与T2I基线(48.4和48.2对48.0)相仿的gFD.
将分配额增加到0.5将有条件的图像符号减少一半(92.2B →\正弦46.1B),分阶段训练的混合效果优于表现(54.2对76.0克/日),虽然在基线上没有改进.
相反地,与中转(1.009 vs 20.437)相比,混合会大大地减少有条件的文本NLL,表明更好的图像标题。
这些结果表明,将培训前预算的一部分分配给I2T作为一项单独的任务,对T2I一代没有好处,尽管标题有所改进.

Across all model sizes, conditional text NLL decreases by more than an order of magnitude (e.g., 18.414 → \rightarrow 1.102 at 0.52B), while gFD, GenEval, and DPG-Bench remain comparable to the baseline (Table 9 ).
Caption alignment also increases with model size (0.090 → \rightarrow 0.559), with qualitative examples from Halcyon -4.00B shown in Figure 6 .

Model scaling and classifier-free guidance. We examine how Halcyon scales from 0.1B to 4B parameters.
Figure 7 shows that both image and text validation NLL decrease consistently with model size, with larger models achieving lower NLL throughout pretraining.

blocks.en:
Implications of language pretraining for T2I generation. Our results challenge the prevailing reliance on internet-scale language pretraining for T2I generation.
In late-fusion systems, pretrained language models provide text representations, but the image generator must learn to map these representations to images using paired data.
On GPIC Test-50K captions, FLAN-T5-XL achieves lower caption NLL than FLAN-T5-Base (2.76 vs. 3.24, averaged over three instruction prompts), with 13.5 × \times more language-pretraining compute ( Chung et al., 2024 ) .
Yet, using FLAN-T5-XL instead of FLAN-T5-Base only modestly improves LlamaGen gFD (66.7 → \rightarrow 63.3).
This result is consistent with Parti ( Yu et al., 2022 ) , which reported marginal benefits from text-encoder pretraining.
For early-fusion models, text-only pretraining optimizes p ⁡ ( 𝒯 ∣ ∅ ) p(\mathcal{T}\mid\varnothing) , whereas T2I generation requires learning p ⁡ ( ℐ ∣ 𝒯 ) p(\mathcal{I}\mid\mathcal{T}) with image tokens produced by an independently trained tokenizer.
Strong text-only modeling therefore does not guarantee a useful initialization for image generation.
Consistent with this view, our randomly initialized Qwen3 model achieves lower vision validation NLL throughout pretraining (Appendix Figure 10 ) and lower final gFD than its language-pretrained counterpart.
In contrast, Halcyon learns text representations for image generation jointly from paired image–text data without language pretraining, although our experiments do not isolate the effect of joint training.
Since our study focuses on pretraining, we account for all pretraining FLOPs required to build each T2I system, including language-model, image-tokenizer, and image-generator pretraining.
We note that our study examines the role of language pretraining in late- and early-fusion systems, not the relative capabilities of autoregressive and diffusion-based image generators.
Beyond T2I, our findings motivate reconsidering the role of modality-specific pretraining in other multimodal settings, including biological data ( Radical Numerics, 2026 ; Neiswanger et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ) .

除了T2I之外,我们的调查结果促使人们重新考虑特定模式的预训在其他多模式环境中的作用,包括生物数据(Rought Numerics,2026;Neiswanger等,2026;Lee等,2026)。

blocks.en:
Limitations and future directions. While our experiments use GPIC, which is, to our knowledge, the largest high-quality, centrally hosted, publicly available dataset and benchmark for visual generation, extending these findings to other datasets and higher resolutions remains important.
Our controlled data composition and scheduling experiments use Halcyon -0.52B, while the pretrained initialization comparison uses Qwen3-0.6B; extensions to larger model sizes and pretraining budgets would help establish the generality of our findings.
Although our late-fusion baselines include diffusion-based generators, our controlled interventions focus on autoregressive models.
Extending these experiments to Transfusion-style models ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) is a valuable direction.
Finally, text-to-video systems such as Wan ( Wan et al., 2025 ) , CogVideoX ( Yang et al., 2025b ) , and Mochi ( Team, 2024 ) also rely on large pretrained language encoders for video generation.
Investigating whether T2V models can learn text conditioning directly from paired video–text data, without language pretraining, is a promising direction toward efficient video generation systems.

blocks.en:
Conclusion. In this work, we study whether internet-scale language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation.
We introduced Halcyon a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models trained entirely from scratch on paired image–text data (GPIC).
Our models outperform strong late-fusion baselines while using significantly less total pretraining compute.
Our controlled experiments show that external text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation under the evaluated settings.
Furthermore, replacing caption-dropped T2I examples with I2T supervision enables image captioning while maintaining competitive generation quality under the same pretraining budget.
Our results show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining.

我们的控制实验显示,在被评价的设置下,外部文本只进行预训并不能改善T2I生成.
此外,将标题投放的T2I实例取而代之的I2T监督可以实现图像标题,同时在相同的预训预算下保持有竞争力的生成质量。

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
Our work studies text-to-image generative modeling, which can be used to generate realistic visual content and may therefore be misused.
By providing a significantly lower-cost recipe for training strong T2I models, our work lowers the barrier to developing capable generative systems, including for malicious use. Halcyon and the baseline models are pretrained on GPIC and may inherit biases or limitations present in its images and captions. Our work does not involve human-subject studies or the collection of a new dataset.
We do not identify additional ethical risks specific to our method beyond those associated with visual generative models.
